Say you are given the following tools:

A tool that searches the internet for relevant API calls.
A tool that executes an API call, in string form.

How would you then go about the process of ordering me a burger and fries from McDonald's.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Below is a high‑level “recipe” for how you could use the two tools you described to place a McDonald’s order for a burger and fries. (Everything is written as a conceptual workflow – you’ll need to adapt it to the actual APIs you discover.) --- ## 1. Gather the necessary information | Step | What you need | Why | |------|---------------|-----| | **User context** | • Delivery address or pickup location
• Payment method (card, Apple Pay, etc.)
• Any special instructions | The API will need a location and a way to charge the customer. | | **Menu items** | • Burger SKU (e.g., “Big Mac”)
• Fries SKU (e.g., “Large Fries”) | You’ll need the exact identifiers that the ordering system uses. | | **Account / auth** | • McDonald’s app credentials or a third‑party service token (UberEats, DoorDash, etc.) | Most ordering APIs require an authenticated session. | --- ## 2. Find the relevant API endpoints 1. **Search for McDonald’s ordering API** ```text search("McDonald's ordering API", "public", "menu", "checkout") ``` *The search tool will return URLs, documentation snippets, or community posts that point to the right endpoints.* 2. **Identify the key endpoints** Typical flow (may vary by region): | Purpose | Example endpoint | Notes | |---------|------------------|-------| | **Get menu** | `/api/v1/menu` | Returns SKUs, prices, modifiers. | | **Create cart** | `/api/v1/cart` | POST with items. | | **Add item** | `/api/v1/cart/items` | POST with SKU, quantity. | | **Set delivery/pickup** | `/api/v1/cart/shipping` | POST with address or store ID. | | **Set payment** | `/api/v1/cart/payment` | POST with tokenized card. | | **Place order** | `/api/v1/orders` | POST finalizes the order. | | **Order status** | `/api/v1/orders/{id}` | GET for tracking. | 3. **Verify authentication flow** *Some APIs use OAuth2, others use a simple bearer token. The search results should reveal the exact flow.* --- ## 3. Build the request payloads ```python # 1️⃣ Create cart cart_payload = { "items": [ {"sku": "BIG_MAC", "quantity": 1}, {"sku": "LARGE_FRIES", "quantity": 1} ] } # 2️⃣ Set delivery address shipping_payload = { "type": "delivery", "address": { "street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip": "90210" } } # 3️⃣ Set payment (tokenized) payment_payload = { "method": "card", "token": "tok_visa_1234567890" } ``` --- ## 4. Execute the API calls Using the **execute API call** tool, you’ll send the requests in the correct order. Below is a simplified example in string form (you’ll replace placeholders with real values). ```text POST https://api.mcdonalds.com/api/v1/cart Headers: Authorization: Bearer , Content-Type: application/json Body: {"items":[{"sku":"BIG_MAC","quantity":1},{"sku":"LARGE_FRIES","quantity":1}]} ``` ```text POST https://api.mcdonalds.com/api/v1/cart/shipping Headers: Authorization: Bearer , Content-Type: application/json Body: {"type":"delivery","address":{"street":"123 Main St","city":"Anytown","state":"CA","zip":"90210"}} ``` ```text POST https://api.mcdonalds.com/api/v1/cart/payment Headers: Authorization: Bearer , Content-Type: application/json Body: {"method":"card","token":"tok_visa_1234567890"} ``` ```text POST https://api.mcdonalds.com/api/v1/orders Headers: Authorization: Bearer , Content-Type: application/json Body: {} # Usually the cart is already finalized; the POST just confirms. ``` --- ## 5. Handle responses & errors | Response | What to do | |----------|------------| | **200 OK** | Extract `order_id`, show confirmation to user. | | **400 Bad Request** | Inspect error message (e.g., invalid SKU, missing address). Prompt user to correct. | | **401 Unauthorized** | Refresh or re‑authenticate token. | | **500 Internal Server Error** | Retry after a short delay; inform user of temporary issue. | --- ## 6. Optional: Track the order ```text GET https://api.mcdonalds.com/api/v1/orders/ Headers: Authorization: Bearer ``` Parse the status (`preparing`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`) and update the UI accordingly. --- ## 7. Wrap‑up 1. **Collect user data** → **Search** → **Find endpoints** → **Build payloads** → **Execute** → **Handle responses** → **Confirm** → **Track**. 2. **Security** – Never log raw payment tokens. Use HTTPS, keep tokens in memory only, and comply with PCI‑DSS if you’re handling card data. 3. **Fallback** – If the McDonald’s API is not publicly available, consider using a third‑party delivery platform (UberEats, DoorDash, etc.) that offers a public SDK or REST interface. --- ### Quick checklist - [ ] Search for McDonald’s or partner API docs. - [ ] Identify authentication method. - [ ] Build cart with correct SKUs. - [ ] Set shipping and payment. - [ ] Place order. - [ ] Confirm and optionally track. That’s the end‑to‑end flow you’d implement with the two tools you mentioned. Happy coding!
